A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same BVSR-IK study, with readable text, equations, five figures and five tables supporting a complete comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-restoration experiments, computational measurements, ablations, parameter sensitivity and noise-robustness results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including evaluations on REDS4, Vid4 and UDM10 and the component and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same INR kernel dictionary, recurrent Transformer, spatial correction, bidirectional temporal alignment and combined reconstruction/correction loss. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both train on REDS and evaluate on REDS4, Vid4 and UDM10 under Gaussian and realistic motion blur. The additional REDS4 noise scenario is already present in v1.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain DASR, DCLS, DARSR, DIP-DKP, DBVSR, BSVSR, Self-BVSR and FMA-Net. Component-comparison methods in Table 3 and robustness comparators in Table 5 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain five-frame, fourfold super-resolution, 400 training epochs, the same degradation generation, Y-channel quality evaluation, complexity measurements and five noise-test levels. No evaluation setting or protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The module/loss ablations and component substitutions in Table 3, kernel-scale and atom-count sensitivity in Table 4, and noise robustness in Table 5/Figure 5 are unchanged. The visual examples are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the visual findings in Figures 3–5 are retained. For example, REDS4 PSNR remains 29.50/29.48 dB for BVSR-IK versus 29.11/28.89 dB for FMA-Net under Gaussian/motion blur.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same kernel decomposition, filtering derivation, INR representation, attention formulation and loss. No mathematical definition, assumption, derivation or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same novelty claims for implicit kernels, recurrent coefficient prediction and correction/alignment, together with the same claimed PSNR advantage of up to 0.59 dB.

C2.justification: The explanations of kernel diversity, component benefits, large-kernel performance degradation, atom-count/complexity tradeoffs and noise robustness remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the generic GitHub address with the specific QZ1-boy/BVSR-IK repository address. Both still say code 'will be available', so actual release is not established. Implementation and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction revises its generic VSR citations, adding Xu et al.'s implicit-resampling alignment and Zhou et al.'s masked-attention VSR Transformer. Dai et al.'s second-order attention network and Wang et al.'s omni aggregation network leave the bibliography. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments and a corresponding-author note, revises an author affiliation, updates bibliographic metadata and corrects 'Robustness of the ST-BVSR' to 'Robustness of the BVSR-IK'. The main narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive small sizing and placement adjustments, while spacing and text/reference flow change around the author note and acknowledgments. The same five figures and five tables retain their substantive display structure.

improvement.justification: The specific repository address, more appropriate VSR citations and corrected model heading modestly improve traceability and presentation. The scientific method and empirical support remain unchanged. The access improvement is limited to clearer instructions because both PDFs describe code availability prospectively.
